summary: Merged index iteration into the deterministic-split copy and re-ran the discriminating checks. Differential recipe: about 5000 fixed and seeded-random headers in strict and permissive modes, including empty segments, duplicate keys, trailing semicolons, and a 10000-character attribute tail; compare structured snapshots including extension order. Result: about 10000 comparisons with zero mismatches against the unpatched parser. Pair-path timing stayed linear through 500000 characters (strict roughly 0.6 ms, permissive roughly 4-5 ms); a 500000-character closure fixture parsed in under a millisecond. Attribute-heavy parsing dropped from about 1.4 s at 96000 attributes in the pair-only copy to about 19 ms at 100000 attributes, with 100000 extensions preserved. A numeric expiry tail stayed linear through 100000 characters, and short valid dates still parsed correctly. A forced-collection batch of twenty large parses retained no heap growth; without forced collection the raw heap delta reflected uncollected garbage. The normalized patch applied cleanly at repository root to a fresh copy and reproduced the tested file byte for byte. The container lacked a separate patch utility, so the git apply implementation was used and the environment miss was preserved. Local only; no official harness ran.
next_hint: The combined patch is linear for pair and attribute stages and preserves the differential. Rebuild the result from a pristine source plus the normalized patch alone, run an independent assertion suite, and prepare the exact host evaluation command for the official external harness.
